text:
maya: FYI: nightly TP end-to-end tests showed a 2–3x step latency spike during warmup on 8xA100. Seems tied to all-reduce bursts when kv-cache fills and we evict small prefixes. flame: https://perf.redwood/1876/warmup-flame :thinking_face:

leo: can you paste the perf snippets? ring vs tree behaviour?

maya: pasted perf tail below. note repeated 1.5–3ms stalls at the same sync points. not CPU-bound.
```
[TP_NODE0][step=12] all_reduce_start -> 0.23ms compute -> wait 2.1ms -> all_reduce_end
[TP_NODE1][step=12] all_reduce_start -> 0.24ms compute -> wait 0.04ms -> all_reduce_end
[TP_NODE2][step=12] all_reduce_start -> 0.22ms compute -> wait 2.3ms -> all_reduce_end
// pattern: node1 fast, others delayed -> imbalanced chunk arrival
```

anya: hmm looks like rendezvous/handshake ordering issue causing small-chunk skew. Have we tried NCCL_ALGO=Tree for small messages?

leo: we did a quick sweep earlier: tree reduces tail latency for sub-8KB messages, but for our current chunking (default chunk_bytes=64KB) we were mostly in ring land. The kicker: kv-cache eviction churn creates a lot of 4–8KB messages during warmup so effective msgsize moves into tree-favorable region.

maya: exact. I repro'd by forcing random evictions on one rank; that rank becomes the bottleneck. Suggestion: coalesce small KV updates client-side OR bump rendezvous chunking for warmup.

infra-bot: deploy-check: profile-agent v2.9 collected extra nccl stats at 1876004500, logs at s3://redwood-perf/tp-warmup/1876004500/

sylvia: small note — NCCL supports an env NCCL_COLLNET_DISABLE and NCCL_TREE_THRESH in some builds. We should test: NCCL_TREE_THRESHOLD=8192 and NCCL_MIN_COLL_SIZE tweaks. Also try NCCL_ALGO=tree + NCCL_PROTO=SIMPLE for <8KB.

matt: +1 test matrix: (A) increase chunk_bytes to 256KB during warmup; (B) enable client coalescing of adjacent small kv deltas up to 64KB; (C) set NCCL_ALGO=tree for warmup only. Will run A/B/C on a 4xTP staging run and attach results.

leo: also instrument comm/compute overlap: add a micro-benchmark where we artificially delay compute on one rank to see whether other ranks backpressure the all-reduce or if ring causes serialization. If ring serializes, you get head-of-line stalls.

maya: quick hack I pushed to runtime: if average message_size < 12KB for last 30s, switch chunk_bytes=128KB and NCCL_ALGO=tree. Prototype lowered 95th by ~30% in local run. Pushed PR #4823 for review.

anya: nice. Can we also add stats emission: per-allreduce msg_size histogram and per-rank wait_time percentiles? That will make regression detection much easier.

matt: agreed. I'll add a Prom counter for nnccl_msgsize_bucket and a gauge for per-rank allreduce_wait_ms. Want alert if p95_wait_ms increases >1.5x baseline across a rollout.

leo: two more hypotheses: (1) rendezvous ordering in our chunk assembler can create skew if one rank flushes earlier; fix by adding a rendezvous sequence id to chunk headers so the reducer can reorder; (2) tcp NIC offload differences cause asymmetric NIC pacing — less likely but we should check pcie util.

maya: noted. For immediate mitigation, I'm toggling warmup policy in dedicated YAML: fast_warmup_coalesce: true + warmup_chunk_bytes: 128KB. Will run scale test at 09:30 PST.

anya: can someone drop the 4-node staging logs here after the run? also include nccl topo dump (nccl-tests --allgather topo) and nvlink/link util.

infra-bot: perf-run complete: 1876005020. Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/tp-warmup/1876005020/. Summary: A (chunk=256KB) improved tail by 25%, B (coalesce) improved by 18%, C (algo=tree) improved by 30% but increased avg token latency by 6% at steady-state.

leo: good signal. We should make warmup-only tree switch, keep steady-state ring for throughput. Also tweak threshold to 12KB not 8KB based on our kv-churn distribution.

maya: filing a follow-up RFC for warmup strategy and metrics: will include coalescing, dynamic chunk sizing, and NCCL-policy toggles. PR/issue refs: #4823, perf/1876005020.

anya: thanks — will add eval prompts to ensure output quality isn't impacted by coalescing. :thumbsup:

matt: leaving a note for eng-sre to watch for regressions in the next deploy window and to keep dedicated customers informed about transient warmup mode.

leo: awesome thread. we should also add a small unit test simulating imbalanced small-chunk arrivals to prevent regressions.

maya: agreed. thanks everyone.
